findings.body: React emits missing-key warnings and cannot correctly reconcile list items as rules stream in incrementally via load-more, potentially reusing component state/DOM across different rules and causing incorrect item rendering.
findings.failure_mode: React list reconciliation errors and console warnings in the filtered rule list.
findings.impact: React emits missing-key warnings and cannot correctly reconcile list items as rules stream in incrementally via load-more, potentially reusing component state/DOM across different rules and causing incorrect item rendering.
findings.root_cause: The key prop was dropped when replacing GrafanaRuleLoader with GrafanaRuleListItem.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `key={key}` on the GrafanaRuleListItem element, mirroring the DataSourceRuleLoader branch.
findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem rendered inside rules.map()
findings.trigger: FilterView renders the filtered rule list; the 'grafana' branch of the switch inside rules.map() no longer passes the `key` prop that the removed GrafanaRuleLoader received (key={key}).
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at FilterView.tsx:157-162 shows GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key prop, while the old GrafanaRuleLoader had `key={key}` (L158 removed). The DataSourceRuleLoader branch at line 165 still has `key={key}`. This is a clear React key omission in a .map() that will cause reconciliation warnings and potential state bugs during incremental loading.

pr.title: Alerting: Remove ruler from alert list view2

raw_findings.body: The menu item is shown (canSilence becomes true via the new grafanaSilenceAbility), but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; the drawer in RuleActionsButtons.V2 is gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) which is false when rulerRule is undefined, so nothing happens. The user sees a visible action that silently does nothing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-visible action that has no effect when triggered from the ruler-free list view.
raw_findings.impact: The menu item is shown (canSilence becomes true via the new grafanaSilenceAbility), but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; the drawer in RuleActionsButtons.V2 is gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) which is false when rulerRule is undefined, so nothing happens. The user sees a visible action that silently does nothing.
raw_findings.root_cause: canSilence now incorporates the prom-rule-based ability, but the downstream silence drawer was not updated to work without a RulerRuleDTO.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer based on the prom rule (accepting a GrafanaPromRuleDTO) when no ruler rule is present, or do not include the grafana ability in canSilence until the drawer supports prom-only rules.
raw_findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op for prom-only rules because SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer still requires a ruler rule
raw_findings.trigger: In the new alert list view, GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule (rulerRule undefined). A user with silence permissions opens the More menu and clicks 'Silence notifications'.

raw_findings.body: The Delete menu item is rendered under the unchanged guard `canDelete && rulerRule &&` and handleDelete requires a RulerRuleDTO, so Delete never appears in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaDeleteAbility is [true, true]. Users lose the ability to delete rules from the list view, and the new grafana delete ability computation is dead code.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Feature regression: delete action silently missing in the new list view; dead ability computation.
raw_findings.impact: The Delete menu item is rendered under the unchanged guard `canDelete && rulerRule &&` and handleDelete requires a RulerRuleDTO, so Delete never appears in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaDeleteAbility is [true, true]. Users lose the ability to delete rules from the list view, and the new grafana delete ability computation is dead code.
raw_findings.root_cause: New prom-rule-based delete ability was added without updating the render guard and delete handler that still depend on rulerRule.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the Delete menu item guard and handleDelete signature to work with a Grafana prom rule identifier (uid) when rulerRule is absent, or remove the grafanaDeleteAbility computation until delete is supported.
raw_findings.title: Delete action is unreachable for prom-only rules despite computing the new grafanaDeleteAbility
raw_findings.trigger: New alert list view renders AlertRuleMenu with promRule only (rulerRule undefined) for a user with AlertingRuleDelete permission.

raw_findings.body: MenuItemPauseRule is gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so pause never renders in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaPauseAbility is [true, true]. Additionally, canPause=true feeds showDivider, so a Menu.Divider can render with no actionable items above it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Feature missing from the new list view plus a cosmetic divider glitch; dead ability computation.
raw_findings.impact: MenuItemPauseRule is gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so pause never renders in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaPauseAbility is [true, true]. Additionally, canPause=true feeds showDivider, so a Menu.Divider can render with no actionable items above it.
raw_findings.root_cause: New prom-rule-based pause ability was added without updating MenuItemPauseRule's rulerRule requirement.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make MenuItemPauseRule accept a Grafana prom rule (or its uid) when rulerRule is absent, or exclude the grafana pause ability from canPause/showDivider until pause supports prom-only rules.
raw_findings.title: Pause action is unreachable for prom-only rules despite computing the new grafanaPauseAbility, causing dead code and a stray menu divider
raw_findings.trigger: New alert list view renders AlertRuleMenu with promRule only (rulerRule undefined) for a user with rule update permission on the folder.

raw_findings.trigger: FilterView renders the filtered rule list; the 'grafana' branch of the switch inside rules.map() no longer passes the `key` prop that the removed GrafanaRuleLoader received (key={key}).

raw_findings.body: The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and marked federated rules immutable. useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (only a TODO), so federated rules now report Update/Delete as supported, exposing Edit/Delete actions that should be disabled and letting users attempt mutations on federated groups.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Federated rules incorrectly appear editable/removable in the UI.
raw_findings.impact: The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and marked federated rules immutable. useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (only a TODO), so federated rules now report Update/Delete as supported, exposing Edit/Delete actions that should be disabled and letting users attempt mutations on federated groups.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor delegated CombinedRule ability computation to a function that lacks access to the rule group and stubs isFederated to false.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass federated-group information into useAllRulerRuleAbilities (e.g., derive it from the group identifier or accept an isFederated flag) instead of hardcoding false, or keep the isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check in useAllAlertRuleAbilities before delegating.
raw_findings.title: useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegation drops the federated rule group immutability check
raw_findings.trigger: A user views a federated Mimir rule group in any view using useAlertRuleAbility/useAllAlertRuleAbilities (e.g., the existing rule list or detail views) with edit/delete permissions.

raw_findings.body: With rule undefined, loading is false and MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, so Duplicate resolves to [true, hasCreatePermission]. canDuplicate in AlertRuleMenu then becomes true via the grafana path even though the ruler-based ability is [false, ...], showing a Duplicate menu item for rules that cannot be duplicated; clicking it triggers a clone flow that fails.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect ability results leak actionable but non-functional menu items for non-Grafana rules.
raw_findings.impact: With rule undefined, loading is false and MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, so Duplicate resolves to [true, hasCreatePermission]. canDuplicate in AlertRuleMenu then becomes true via the grafana path even though the ruler-based ability is [false, ...], showing a Duplicate menu item for rules that cannot be duplicated; clicking it triggers a clone flow that fails.
raw_findings.root_cause: The skipToken/undefined-rule path still computes supported flags as AlwaysSupported rather than NotSupported.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Short-circuit useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to return all-NotSupported abilities when rule is undefined, instead of computing supported flags from an absent rule.
raw_findings.title: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities reports actions as supported when rule is undefined (skipToken)
raw_findings.trigger: AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons call useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities with skipToken for non-Grafana rules (e.g., a vanilla Prometheus data source rule without a ruler API) while the user holds Grafana rule create permission.

raw_findings.body: The replaced GrafanaRuleLoader built the href with createReturnTo() (`createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })`); the new component omits it, so the rule detail page loses the returnTo query parameter and can no longer navigate back to the exact list/filter state the user came from.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Navigation regression: back/return-to context lost after opening a rule from the list.
raw_findings.impact: The replaced GrafanaRuleLoader built the href with createReturnTo() (`createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })`); the new component omits it, so the rule detail page loses the returnTo query parameter and can no longer navigate back to the exact list/filter state the user came from.
raw_findings.root_cause: returnTo handling was not carried over when GrafanaRuleListItem was extracted from GrafanaRuleLoader.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reintroduce createReturnTo() and pass { returnTo } to createRelativeUrl when building the view href.
raw_findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter from the rule view link
raw_findings.trigger: User clicks a Grafana rule name in the new list view (grouped or filtered) to open the rule detail page, then uses the return-to-previous navigation.

raw_findings.body: The stray '// duplicate' note conveys no meaning (nothing is duplicated on that line) and looks like an unfinished refactoring marker, reducing code clarity in a permissions-critical hook.
raw_findings.evidence: const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate
raw_findings.failure_mode: Confusing dead comment in reviewed code.
raw_findings.impact: The stray '// duplicate' note conveys no meaning (nothing is duplicated on that line) and looks like an unfinished refactoring marker, reducing code clarity in a permissions-critical hook.
raw_findings.root_cause: Development scratch comment committed with the new hook.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the '// duplicate' comment or replace it with an explanatory comment if it was meant to flag intentional duplication of useIsRuleEditable logic.
raw_findings.title: Leftover '// duplicate' comment on useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call
raw_findings.trigger: Any reader or reviewer of useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities encounters the trailing comment.

raw_findings.body: The test asserts the exact absence of the Delete menu item even though the user has delete permissions, silently enshrining the list-view delete regression; if delete support is later restored, the brittle exact-count assertion will fail for the wrong reason.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test masks a functional regression and is brittle to legitimate menu changes.
raw_findings.impact: The test asserts the exact absence of the Delete menu item even though the user has delete permissions, silently enshrining the list-view delete regression; if delete support is later restored, the brittle exact-count assertion will fail for the wrong reason.
raw_findings.root_cause: Exact-count assertion written against current (regressed) behavior rather than intended permission-driven behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assert the presence/absence of each expected menu item explicitly (including an explicit expectation and comment about Delete being unsupported in the ruler-free list view) instead of an exact total count.
raw_findings.title: New test hard-codes exactly 4 menu items, baking in the missing Delete action for a user with delete permission
raw_findings.trigger: Running GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx: the beforeEach grants AlertingRuleDelete and folder delete access control, yet the menu assertion counts only silence/copy-link/duplicate/export.

However, examining the code flow: when rule is undefined, isEditable and isRemovable would be undefined/false, and the abilities use these values directly (lines 320-321). The Duplicate ability uses duplicateSupported which depends on isPluginProvided check that handles undefined rule. The claim about canDuplicate becoming true is not fully substantiated - the permission check still applies.

finding.suggested_fix: Assert the presence/absence of each expected menu item explicitly (including an explicit expectation and comment about Delete being unsupported in the ruler-free list view) instead of an exact total count.

validated_findings.body: The menu item is shown (canSilence becomes true via the new grafanaSilenceAbility), but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; the drawer in RuleActionsButtons.V2 is gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) which is false when rulerRule is undefined, so nothing happens. The user sees a visible action that silently does nothing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: User-visible action that has no effect when triggered from the ruler-free list view.
validated_findings.impact: The menu item is shown (canSilence becomes true via the new grafanaSilenceAbility), but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; the drawer in RuleActionsButtons.V2 is gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) which is false when rulerRule is undefined, so nothing happens. The user sees a visible action that silently does nothing.
validated_findings.root_cause: canSilence now incorporates the prom-rule-based ability, but the downstream silence drawer was not updated to work without a RulerRuleDTO.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer based on the prom rule (accepting a GrafanaPromRuleDTO) when no ruler rule is present, or do not include the grafana ability in canSilence until the drawer supports prom-only rules.
validated_findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op for prom-only rules because SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer still requires a ruler rule
validated_findings.trigger: In the new alert list view, GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule (rulerRule undefined). A user with silence permissions opens the More menu and clicks 'Silence notifications'.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is correct per RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104, but the patch shows canSilence now includes grafanaSilenceAbility which uses useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport and useCanSilenceInFolder (lines 292-293 in useAbilities.ts). The drawer guard requires rulerRule, but the finding assumes the menu item will show without the drawer working. However, the silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu.tsx:126-131 only calls handleSilence which sets showSilenceDrawer - the drawer rendering is in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104-106 which does require rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). This is a valid concern but the trigger scenario is speculative - we cannot confirm from the patch that GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule without rulerRule in a way that triggers this exact path.

validated_findings.body: The Delete menu item is rendered under the unchanged guard `canDelete && rulerRule &&` and handleDelete requires a RulerRuleDTO, so Delete never appears in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaDeleteAbility is [true, true]. Users lose the ability to delete rules from the list view, and the new grafana delete ability computation is dead code.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Feature regression: delete action silently missing in the new list view; dead ability computation.
validated_findings.impact: The Delete menu item is rendered under the unchanged guard `canDelete && rulerRule &&` and handleDelete requires a RulerRuleDTO, so Delete never appears in the ruler-free list view even when grafanaDeleteAbility is [true, true]. Users lose the ability to delete rules from the list view, and the new grafana delete ability computation is dead code.
validated_findings.root_cause: New prom-rule-based delete ability was added without updating the render guard and delete handler that still depend on rulerRule.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the Delete menu item guard and handleDelete signature to work with a Grafana prom rule identifier (uid) when rulerRule is absent, or remove the grafanaDeleteAbility computation until delete is supported.
validated_findings.title: Delete action is unreachable for prom-only rules despite computing the new grafanaDeleteAbility
validated_findings.trigger: New alert list view renders AlertRuleMenu with promRule only (rulerRule undefined) for a user with AlertingRuleDelete permission.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule &&` is confirmed in AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165. However, the finding claims this is a regression - the patch adds grafanaDeleteAbility computation but the render guard was already requiring rulerRule before this patch. The patch doesn't change the render guard, so this is pre-existing behavior, not a patch-introduced bug. The new ability computation may be intentionally for future use.

validated_findings.title: Pause action is unreachable for prom-only rules despite computing the new grafanaPauseAbility, causing dead code and a stray menu divider

validated_findings.body: React emits missing-key warnings and cannot correctly reconcile list items as rules stream in incrementally via load-more, potentially reusing component state/DOM across different rules and causing incorrect item rendering.

validated_findings.root_cause: The key prop was dropped when replacing GrafanaRuleLoader with GrafanaRuleListItem.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore `key={key}` on the GrafanaRuleListItem element, mirroring the DataSourceRuleLoader branch.
validated_findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem rendered inside rules.map()
validated_findings.trigger: FilterView renders the filtered rule list; the 'grafana' branch of the switch inside rules.map() no longer passes the `key` prop that the removed GrafanaRuleLoader received (key={key}).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at FilterView.tsx:157-162 shows GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key prop, while the old GrafanaRuleLoader had `key={key}` (L158 removed). The DataSourceRuleLoader branch at line 165 still has `key={key}`. This is a clear React key omission in a .map() that will cause reconciliation warnings and potential state bugs during incremental loading.

validated_findings.body: The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and marked federated rules immutable. useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (only a TODO), so federated rules now report Update/Delete as supported, exposing Edit/Delete actions that should be disabled and letting users attempt mutations on federated groups.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass federated-group information into useAllRulerRuleAbilities (e.g., derive it from the group identifier or accept an isFederated flag) instead of hardcoding false, or keep the isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check in useAllAlertRuleAbilities before delegating.

validated_findings.trigger: A user views a federated Mimir rule group in any view using useAlertRuleAbility/useAllAlertRuleAbilities (e.g., the existing rule list or detail views) with edit/delete permissions.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding claims useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegation drops federated rule check. Looking at useAbilities.ts:228, useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities. The old code had `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` but the new useAllRulerRuleAbilities at line 245 has `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO comment. However, useAllAlertRuleAbilities is marked @deprecated (line 220) and the federated check was already a TODO in the old code. The patch context doesn't show the old implementation had working federated detection that was removed.
